question: Mahesh has ₹1617 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Vijay and Ajay and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Vijay and Ajay got same amount after 19 and 20 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Mahesh give to Vijay?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal after different times, the person with less time gets more principal to start with.

Ratio of Vijay's to Ajay's share = (100 + R) / 100 raised to the difference in time.

Vijay : Ajay = (110/100)²⁰ − ¹⁹ = 11 : 10

Vijay's share = (11 ÷ 21) × 1617 = 847

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total principal = ₹1617

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Vijay = 19 years

Time for Ajay = 20 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P(1 + R/100)T
